<p>Compare the original movie with a base difference and a running difference. Pause or move one frame at a time to follow a feature. These are changes in rendered colour images; no shock type has been assigned.</p>
<p class="legend"><strong>Black</strong>: a decrease <span class="tone" aria-hidden="true"></span><strong>White</strong>: an increase. Midgray: no change. Each difference panel uses one fixed scale through the sequence.</p>
<p class="muted">51 cropped preview frames · order 00–50. Playback delay is not the observing cadence.</p>
<details><summary>How these views were made, and what they can tell us</summary><div class="method">
<ul><li>We subtract a weighted brightness from the displayed RGB image: L = 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B. This is not calibrated EUV intensity; the movie’s colour mapping and original intensity scaling are unknown.</li>
<li>Before subtraction, each brightness image receives the same Gaussian spatial smoothing, sigma = 2 pixels. There is no temporal smoothing. This reduces fine image grain; it does not recover missing resolution.</li>
<li>The base is frame 00, the first supplied frame. It has not been verified as a pre-event image. The running view uses a separation of one or three image indices.</li>
<li>Display limits are ±14 brightness-code units for the base view, ±6 for adjacent frames and ±9 for a three-frame separation. Strong changes are clipped to black or white. Different panels therefore do not share an amplitude scale.</li>
<li>No extra derotation, image shift, exposure correction or frame-by-frame normalization has been applied. Prior motion compensation is possible but not documented in these JPEGs; exact image alignment has not been certified.</li>
<li>A changing feature, a displaced structure, exposure differences and residual registration errors can all produce bright/dark patterns. This review helps locate candidate features. It supplies no density jump, plasma velocity, magnetic field or MHD classification.</li></ul>
<p><strong>Source:</strong> NOAA/GOES-16 SUVI 195 Å · 10 September 2017. Cropped JPEG excerpt of the <a href="https://www.goes-r.gov/multimedia/dataAndImageryVideosGoes-16.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">official NOAA animation</a> (credit: NOAA SWPC). Display processing: RMO. For detailed observations and processing, see <a href="https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/aaa28e" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Seaton &amp; Darnel (2018)</a>.</p>
<p>These rendered preview images are for visual comparison. Calibrated intensities, exposure corrections and observation times must be obtained from the instrument data for quantitative work.</p>
